title: Registries and Routine Outcome Data — Learning From Every Patient

hook.en: Every day a clinic generates data that could answer big questions: who recovers, how long it takes and what helps. Most of it is lost in paper files. A registry turns routine care into evidence, and routine outcome measures turn each patient into part of a bigger story.
hook.ur: Har din clinic aisa data paida karta hai jo bade sawalon ka jawab de sakta hai: kaun theek hota hai, kitna waqt lagta hai aur kya madad karta hai. Zyada tar kaghazi files mein kho jata hai. Registry routine care ko saboot mein badalti hai, aur routine outcome measures har mareez ko bari kahani ka hissa banate hain.

goal.en: By the end, you'll explain what a patient registry is, choose a small set of routine outcomes, know the strengths and limits of registry data, and plan simple, ethical data collection in your own clinic.
goal.ur: End tak aap samjhayenge ke patient registry kya hai, routine outcomes ka chhota set chunenge, registry data ki khoobiyan aur hadein jaanenge, aur apne clinic mein saada, akhlaqi data collection plan karenge.

text.en: A **registry** is an organised system that collects uniform data on patients with a particular condition, treatment or exposure, to answer defined questions. **Routine outcome measurement** means recording the same few measures for every patient at set times, such as a pain and function score at the start, at discharge and at three months. Registry data show what happens in **real practice** with all kinds of patients, but without a comparison group, they are open to bias.
text.ur: **Registry** ek munazzam nizam hai jo khaas halat, ilaaj ya exposure wale mareezon ka ek jaisa data jama karta hai taake tay shuda sawalon ka jawab de. **Routine outcome measurement** ka matlab har mareez ke liye tay waqton par wohi chand naap record karna hai, jaise shuru, discharge aur teen mahine par dard aur function ka score. Registry data **haqeeqi practice** mein har qism ke mareezon ke saath kya hota hai dikhata hai, lekin comparison group ke baghair bias ka shikar ho sakta hai.

text.en: Think of **a school record book**. A single child's marks tell you little. The whole school's records over years tell you which methods work, which classes need help and whether results improve. A registry is the record book of a clinic or a country.
text.ur: **School ki report book** sochein. Ek bache ke number kam batate hain. Saalon ka poore school ka record batata hai kaun se tareeqe kaam karte hain, kin classon ko madad chahiye aur nateeje behtar ho rahe hain ya nahi. Registry clinic ya mulk ki report book hai.

title.en: Strengths and limits of registry and routine data
title.ur: Registry aur routine data ki khoobiyan aur hadein

rows.en: Real, varied patients, including older and complex ones usually excluded from trials
rows.ur: Haqeeqi, mukhtalif mareez, un buzurgon aur pechida mareezon samet jo aam taur par trials se bahar hote hain

rows.en: Only people who reach the service, so some groups are missing
rows.ur: Sirf woh jo service tak pohanchte hain, isliye kuch group ghayab

rows.en: Large numbers and long follow-up at modest cost
rows.ur: Bade numbers aur lamba follow-up mamooli kharch par

rows.en: Data may be incomplete or recorded inconsistently
rows.ur: Data adhoora ya be-qaida record ho sakta hai

rows.en: Good for describing outcomes, variation and rare harms
rows.ur: Nateeje, farq aur nadir nuqsan bayan karne ke liye achha

rows.en: No randomisation, so cannot prove a treatment caused the result
rows.ur: Randomisation nahi, isliye sabit nahi kar sakta ke ilaaj ne nateeja diya

rows.en: Lets clinics compare their results with others and spot gaps
rows.ur: Clinics ko apne nateeje doosron se milane aur kami dhoondhne deta hai

rows.en: Needs case-mix adjustment, or comparisons can be unfair
rows.ur: Case-mix adjustment chahiye, warna muqabla na-munsifana ho sakta hai

title.en: Starting routine outcomes in a clinic
title.ur: Clinic mein routine outcomes shuru karna

steps.title: Choose few, meaningful measures
steps.detail: Pick two or three that matter to patients and are quick to complete, for example a pain score, a function score and one patient-chosen goal. || Chand, ba-maani naap chunein

steps.title: Fix when to collect
steps.detail: For example at the first visit, at discharge and at three months. Make it part of the routine, not an extra. || Jama karne ka waqt tay karein

steps.title: Record consistently and securely
steps.detail: Use the same form or spreadsheet, a patient code instead of a name, and a safe place for the data. || Mustaqil aur mehfooz tareeqe se record karein

steps.title: Look at the data regularly
steps.detail: Review a summary every few months: average change, proportion improved beyond the MCID, and who is not improving. || Data ko baqaidgi se dekhein

steps.title: Act on it
steps.detail: Use findings to improve care, share them with patients in plain language and report them honestly. || Us par amal karein

question.en: A clinic records pain and function scores for every back pain patient at the start and at discharge, and finds average improvement. What can it NOT say?
question.ur: Ek clinic har peeth dard ke mareez ka shuru aur discharge par dard aur function ka score record karta hai aur average behtari paata hai. Woh kya NAHI keh sakta?

feedback.ur: Routine data yeh keh sakta hai.

text.en: What the average starting score was

feedback.ur: Routine data yeh keh sakta hai.

text.en: That the clinic's treatment caused the improvement, because there is no comparison group and many patients recover anyway
text.ur: Ke clinic ke ilaaj ne behtari ki, kyunke comparison group nahi aur bohat se mareez waise bhi theek ho jate hain

feedback.en: Yes — routine data describe outcomes but cannot prove cause.
feedback.ur: Haan — routine data nateeje bayan karte hain lekin wajah sabit nahi kar sakte.

question.en: Why might comparing two clinics' registry results be unfair without adjustment?
question.ur: Adjustment ke baghair do clinics ke registry nateeje milana na-munsifana kyun ho sakta hai?

text.en: One clinic always uses better scales
text.ur: Ek clinic hamesha behtar scales istemal karta hai

feedback.en: Both should use the same measures.
feedback.ur: Dono ko wohi naap istemal karne chahiye.

text.en: Their patients may differ in age, severity and other factors (case-mix), which affects outcomes regardless of care quality
text.ur: Un ke mareez umar, shiddat aur doosre factors (case-mix) mein mukhtalif ho sakte hain, jo care ki quality se alag nateeje par asar karte hain

feedback.en: Yes — adjustment for case-mix makes comparisons fairer.
feedback.ur: Haan — case-mix adjustment muqabla zyada munsifana banata hai.

question.en: Which is the best approach to consent and privacy for routine data?
question.ur: Routine data ke liye razamandi aur nijiyat ka behtareen tareeqa kaun sa hai?

text.en: Tell patients what is collected and why, use codes instead of names, store the data securely, and follow local rules for consent
text.ur: Mareezon ko batayein kya jama ho raha hai aur kyun, naam ke bajaye codes istemal karein, data mehfooz rakhein aur razamandi ke muqami qaide follow karein

feedback.en: Yes — transparency and protection build trust.
feedback.ur: Haan — shaffafiyat aur hifazat bharosa banati hai.

text.en: Collect everything in case it is useful later
text.ur: Sab kuch jama karein kya pata baad mein kaam aaye

feedback.ur: Sirf wohi jama karein jo chahiye.

text.en: Share named records with anyone who asks
text.ur: Naam wale records kisi ko bhi dein jo maange

text.en: **Collecting data nobody uses.** A registry that grows without anyone looking at it is a waste, and a burden for patients. Start small, make sure every item has a purpose, and look at results regularly. Another trap is cherry-picking: reporting only patients who completed follow-up flatters your results, so report how many were lost.
text.ur: **Aisa data jama karna jo koi istemal na kare.** Registry jo kisi ke dekhe baghair barhti rahe zaya hai, aur mareezon par bojh. Chhote se shuru karein, yaqeeni banayein ke har item ka maqsad ho, aur nateeje baqaidgi se dekhein. Ek aur jaal chun-chun kar lena hai: sirf follow-up mukammal karne walay mareezon ki report aap ke nateejon ko achha dikhati hai, isliye batayein kitne chhoot gaye.

text.en: **Make it quick.** A two-minute questionnaire on a tablet or on paper, scored automatically, is more likely to become routine than a long form. Share the patient's own change on a simple graph, which can motivate them and open the conversation about goals. In Pakistan, a simple Urdu form and a locked cabinet or a password-protected spreadsheet are a sound start.
text.ur: **Isay tez rakhein.** Tablet ya kaagaz par do minute ka questionnaire, khud-ba-khud score hota hua, lambe form se zyada routine ban-ne ka imkaan rakhta hai. Mareez ki apni tabdeeli saade graph par dikhayein, jo unhein hausla de sakti hai aur maqasid par baat shuru karti hai. Pakistan mein saada Urdu form aur taale wali almari ya password wali spreadsheet achha aaghaz hai.

question.en: Can a registry ever tell us whether a treatment works?
question.ur: Kya registry kabhi bata sakti hai ke ilaaj kaam karta hai?

answer.en: Registry data alone are limited, but some newer designs embed randomisation in a registry (registry-based randomised trials), which gives real-world data and fair comparison at lower cost. Registries are also excellent for spotting unusually good or bad results and rare harms that trials are too small to detect.
answer.ur: Sirf registry data mehdood hain, lekin kuch naye designs registry mein randomisation shamil karte hain (registry-based randomised trials), jo kam kharch par haqeeqi duniya ka data aur munsifana muqabla dete hain. Registries ghair mamooli taur par achhe ya bure nateeje aur nadir nuqsan pakadne ke liye bhi behtareen hain jinhein trials dhoondhne ke liye bohat chhote hote hain.

beats.patient: A group of physiotherapists in three cities start recording the same two-minute shoulder questionnaire and a goal rating at the first visit, at six weeks and at three months, using coded forms.
beats.assessment: After a year, they see that patients with high baseline fear of movement improve less and are more often lost to follow-up.
beats.treatment: The group adds a short conversation about fear and activity at the first visit, and tracks whether the results change over six months.
beats.reassess: The next year's data show better improvement and fewer drop-outs in that group, and they present the findings at a national meeting.

text.en: **Collect only what you need, and keep it safe.** Health data are sensitive. Limit who can see them, keep them off personal phones and shared drives, delete data when no longer needed and never use them for anything patients were not told about. Check the data-protection rules of your country and employer.
text.ur: **Sirf jo chahiye jama karein, aur mehfooz rakhein.** Sehat ka data hassas hai. Dekhne walon ko mehdood karein, nijji phones aur shared drives se door rakhein, zaroorat na rahe to data mitayein aur usay aise kaam mein kabhi istemal na karein jis ke baare mein mareezon ko na bataya gaya ho. Apne mulk aur idare ke data protection qaide dekhein.

text.en: The AHRQ guide to patient registries describes registries as organised systems that use observational methods to collect uniform data to evaluate specified outcomes for a defined population, and discusses planning, data quality, ethics and uses such as describing natural history, measuring effectiveness and monitoring safety. A paper in the BMJ on patient-reported outcome measures in practice argued that routine collection can improve care when results are shared with clinicians and patients, but that systems must be simple and results actionable.
text.ur: AHRQ ki patient registries ki rehnumai registries ko aise munazzam nizam batati hai jo observational tareeqon se ek jaisa data jama karte hain taake ek tay shuda aabadi ke tay shuda nateeje parakhe, aur plan, data ki quality, akhlaqiyat aur istemal jaise qudrati tareekh bayan karna, effectiveness naapna aur safety nigrani par baat karti hai. BMJ ke ek paper ne patient-reported outcome measures par daleel di ke routine jama karna care behtar kar sakta hai jab nateeje clinicians aur mareezon se share hon, lekin nizam saada aur nateeje amal ke qabil hone chahiyen.

text.en: **Few, Same, Safe, Used.** Few measures, same each time, safely stored, and actually used.
text.ur: **Chand, Wohi, Mehfooz, Istemal.** Chand naap, har baar wohi, mehfooz zakhira, aur sach mein istemal.

summary.en: Registries and routine outcomes show what happens in real practice, but without comparison groups they cannot prove cause.
summary.ur: Registries aur routine outcomes haqeeqi practice mein kya hota hai dikhate hain, lekin comparison groups ke baghair wajah sabit nahi kar sakte.

summary.en: Choose a few meaningful measures, collect them at set times, and compare clinics only after adjusting for case-mix.
summary.ur: Chand ba-maani naap chunein, tay waqton par jama karein, aur clinics ko sirf case-mix adjust karne ke baad milayein.

summary.en: Keep the data simple, secure and used, and report lost follow-up honestly.
summary.ur: Data saada, mehfooz aur istemal mein rakhein, aur chhootay follow-up ki imaandari se report karein.

back.en: An organised system collecting uniform data on patients with a condition or treatment.
back.ur: Munazzam nizam jo kisi halat ya ilaaj wale mareezon ka ek jaisa data jama kare.

back.en: The mix of patient age, severity and other factors that affects outcomes.
back.ur: Umar, shiddat aur doosre factors ka mel jo nateejon par asar daalta hai.

front.en: Can routine data prove a treatment works?
front.ur: Kya routine data sabit kar sakta hai ke ilaaj kaam karta hai?

back.en: No; there is no comparison group.

front.ur: Follow-up ke chhootne ki report kyun?

back.en: Reporting only completers flatters the results.
back.ur: Sirf mukammal karne walon ki report nateeje achhe dikhati hai.

note.en: Using routine data to improve care.
note.ur: Care behtar karne ke liye routine data ka istemal.
